questions.question: Which description fits the **TerminologyCapabilities** resource?
options: This resource documents a set of capabilities (behaviors) of a FHIR Terminology Server that may be used as a statement of actual server functionality or a statement of required or desired server…
This resource is used to declare the existence of and describe a code system or code system supplement and its key properties, and optionally define a part or all of its content.
A statement of relationships from one set of concepts to one or more other concepts - either concepts in code systems, or data element/data element concepts, or classes in class models.
A curated namespace that issues unique symbols within that namespace for the identification of concepts, people, devices, etc.
questions.explanation: **TerminologyCapabilities**: A TerminologyCapabilities resource documents a set of capabilities (behaviors) of a FHIR Terminology Server that may be used as a statement of actual server functionality or a statement of required or desired server implementation. The other descriptions belong to **CodeSystem**, **ConceptMap**, **NamingSystem**.

questions.question: Which resource matches this definition from the specification? “This resource documents a set of capabilities (behaviors) of a FHIR Terminology Server that may be used as a statement of actual server functionality or a statement of required or desired server…”
questions.explanation: This is the definition of **TerminologyCapabilities** (Foundation › Terminology).

questions.question: Where does **TerminologyCapabilities** sit in the FHIR R4 resource list?
questions.explanation: **TerminologyCapabilities** is in **Foundation › Terminology**: Define and manage codes: code systems, value sets that choose the codes allowed in a field, mappings between code systems, and what a terminology server supports.

questions.question: Which element is **required** (minimum cardinality 1) in every **TerminologyCapabilities** instance?
questions.explanation: The required top-level elements of TerminologyCapabilities are `status` (1..1), `date` (1..1), `kind` (1..1). The other options have a minimum cardinality of 0, so they are optional.

questions.question: Which element of **TerminologyCapabilities** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of TerminologyCapabilities: `status`. `status`: draft | active | retired | unknown. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource: for example, a status of `entered-in-error` means the data must not be used.
